chapter: Hopkins, Kelly's Stables and Red Allen
title: Adrian Rollini and Lionel Hampton as vibraphonists
summary: At Bill Mather's drum shop he learned vibes fingering from Adrian Rollini, whom he considered the best vibist; he preferred Hampton as a drummer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Milt. I had heard -- well, I used to play with Adrian Rollini (PHONETIC) and --
All those guys you know. We used to go down and rehearse with his wife, Dixie, you know, and they were all good friends of mine.
Oh, yeah. And because Adrian played vibraphones and the bass saxophone.

You know. So we used to rehearse a lot at this Bill Mather's place. He had a drum shop there. So we would all hang out there in Bill's shop, you know. And Adrian and I became real tight, because he'd show me things. "Wait a minute, kid, let me show you how that goes." "Let me show you the fingering." You know? Because I used to have trouble getting real fast going up the vibes.
So he would show me really the technical way to do it.
So he'd say, "Now, you do this." And I'd say, "Oh, yeah, wonderful." You know? And, "Oh, yeah, beautiful."
And I had been listening to Lionel Hampton, but I liked him better as a drummer.
And that's what I -- vibraphones with Lionel, I never paid much attention to.
Always listened to his drumming, which I thought was fantastic, you know?
And he was so -- he could do so many things with his hands, you know, he could -- like he would just like -- the sticks became his sixth finger.
Oh, he was a fantastic drummer. And I always thought Adrian was the best vibraphone player I'd ever heard. And then through Bill I became close to Adrian.
So I said, 'Well, this is my man.'
So I used to bring Freddie Greene to play guitar with us.
Used to have a wonderful time with Adrian.
No kidding. That's nice to know. I didn't know anything about that.
Well, Milton was very close with Mildred
She'd come on and sing, 'Mildred Bailey and her rocking chair. Rock, rock.'
